channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln’s long Iran mission sparks alarm: Hegseth rejects reports of poor conditions of sailors
item.description: The Lincoln's deployment has included more than 240 consecutive days at sea, one of the longest uninterrupted periods for a US aircraft carrier in recent years.

item.title: Trump’s $20,000 US visa bond rule may expand beyond 50 countries; travel industry warns it could hurt tourism, economy
item.description: The US Department of State this month made permanent a visa bond programme that was initially introduced as a pilot in August 2025.

item.title: US colleges face 1.1 lakh drop in foreign students in 2026 amid stricter visa rules; what Indian students need to know
item.description: Changes to US visa policies, processing priorities and rules governing student stays could have a disproportionate impact on Indians seeking admission to American universities.

item.title: Uttarakhand tunnel collapse: 6 dead, 14 injured after water and debris trap workers in Chamoli — updates
item.description: A rescue operation is ongoing in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district after water and debris trapped workers in a tunnel at a hydroelectric site. Although 16 workers have been saved, efforts continue. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami emphasises prioritising safe evacuations.

item.title: A ban on an entire batch and a U-turn later, Bar Council seeks Nalsar report on anti-CJI campaign
item.description: The Bar Council of India withdrew its blanket enrolment ban on Nalsar’s 2026 graduating batch within hours, easing uncertainty for students and employers. But it is pressing ahead with its inquiry into the campaign opposing Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s participation in the convocation.

item.title: Hegseth says US can maintain Iran blockade ‘indefinitely’ as Strait of Hormuz standoff deepens
item.description: Hegseth said the US Navy could keep ships in the region for as long as necessary by rotating vessels in and out of the area.

item.title: State Bank of India raises $500 million via bonds in overseas market; issue attracts $2.46 billion orders
item.description: The 'Regulation S' bond is benchmarked against the 5-year US Treasury and priced at a spread of 88 bps over the benchmark, SBI said in a statement on Thursday.

item.title: Delhi man stunned as cab driver speaks fluent English, reveals he learnt it using ChatGPT
item.description: The conversation continued for nearly 10 minutes, with the driver speaking in English while Tushar Jejani responded in Hindi. It was only after Jejani asked about the phone call that he discovered what the driver had actually been doing.

item.title: Assam-Arunachal border dispute explained: History, 2023 pact and why tensions persist
item.description: The Assam-Arunachal border dispute dates back to colonial-era demarcation and has persisted despite the 2023 settlement. Fresh clashes highlight unresolved land and boundary claims, with 52 disputed areas still remaining.

item.title: India, US in 'regular contact' on trade deal, says commerce secretary Agrawal
item.description: Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said both sides remain committed to the February framework even as Washington weighs further tariff action and probes India’s trade practices.

item.title: Russia says Putin’s secret train doesn’t exist: Leaked docs reveal what’s inside; beauty salon, Turkish bath and more
item.description: Leaked documents reveal details of Vladimir Putin's luxurious private train, featuring a gym, spa and steam bath. Construction ties to Kremlin officials suggest tight security around its use.

item.title: Ebola outbreak in Congo: 4,500+ infected, 2,100 dead; WHO warns of potentially deadliest epidemic ever
item.description: The development comes as the World Health Organization warns that the outbreak in eastern Congo could become the deadliest Ebola epidemic in history.

item.title: BCI withdraws NALSAR enrolment ban hours after barring 2026 graduates over CJI convocation campaign
item.description: Hours after halting enrolment of NALSAR's 2026 law graduates over an alleged CJI convocation campaign, BCI modified its order, allowing all students to enrol. It said most students were innocent and will not suffer.

item.title: Record heatwave grips Asia as potatoes ‘boil’ in fields, lions perish
item.description: The crop, grown in South Korea’s Gangwon province, had appeared healthy just a week earlier. But when Lee dug into the soil, he found the potatoes were ‘like boiled potatoes’.

item.title: Japan condemns Putin’s visit to Kuril Islands: What is the dispute about?
item.description: Putin visited Iturup, one of the southern Kuril Islands, on Thursday (August 13). Japan claims the island, which it calls Etorofu, as part of its Northern Territories. Tokyo described the visit as “absolutely unacceptable” and formally protested to Russia.

item.title: West Bengal: BJP’s Rajya Sabha MP loses top honour over ‘derogatory’ remarks against Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
item.description: West Bengal has revoked the Banga Bibhushan award from Nagendra Ray, known as Ananta Maharaj, effective immediately. The decision follows controversial comments he made about Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.&nbsp;

item.title: Who is Mirza Fakhrul? BNP nominates party's secretary general for presidential election in Bangladesh
item.description: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party nominated Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as its presidential candidate on Thursday, ahead of the August 20 election. He resigned as secretary general and from the Standing Committee following his nomination, as announced by senior party official Ruhul Kabir Rizvi.

item.title: In a first, govt plans turning citizen grievances into a source of policy reforms
item.description: The government will for the first time systematically mine citizen grievances and suggestions from platforms like CPGRAMS and the PMO portal to identify recurring gaps and convert them into policy reforms.&nbsp;

item.title: Birth tourism crackdown: US revokes more than 600 visas; Marco Rubio says ‘American citizenship is not for sale’
item.description: The visa cancellations followed the creation of a Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force by State Department to identify people allegedly abusing the US visa system, dismantle networks facilitating birth tourism and prevent what the administration describes as the exploitation of US citizenship laws.

item.title: ‘Devastated’: Teenage Australian golfer Jessica Bang dies in Bangkok; tributes pour in
item.description: Australian golfer Jessica Bang, 18, has died in Bangkok after suffering a brain haemorrhage. Her family confirmed her passing on 13 August.&nbsp;

item.title: Karoline Leavitt successor: Alina Habba, Matt Boyle, Steven Cheung among names in race for White House press secretary
item.description: Several names are now being discussed within Trump’s orbit, with Alina Habba and Breitbart Washington Bureau Chief Matthew Boyle emerging as early contenders, according to The New York Post, which cited sources within the administration.

item.title: US vs Iran over Strait of Hormuz: Who controls the world’s vital waterway nearly half a year into war?
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains contested as the US and Iran dispute control over the critical waterway. US claims of dominance are rejected by Iran, which insists it retains authority. The US naval blockade effectively halted its maritime trade through the strategic waterway.

item.title: E20 petrol controversy | India's top carmakers privately raise serious concerns about fuel contamination: Report
item.description: India's top carmakers, including Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors and Mahindra, have expressed private concerns about E20 petrol contamination, according to Reuters.&nbsp;

item.title: 'We have learned how to fight America': What IRGC's Mohammad Reza Naqdi said about Iran's long-term war strategy
item.description: IRGC General Mohammad Reza Naqdi said Iran has learned how to fight the US during five months of war and could prolong the conflict until 2029 to build deterrence. He also claimed Iran can sustain missile production for years.

item.title: On 15th August, 2026, is India celebrating the 79th Independence Day or 80th? Explained
item.description: The confusion comes from how the celebrations are counted. India’s first Independence Day was observed on August 15, 1947. From then on, each year’s celebration adds to the count.

item.title: Independence day parade tickets 2026: How to do online booking for celebrations at Red Fort on 15 August? Check details
item.description: To attend the Independence Day ceremony at Delhi's Red Fort, book entry passes online through the Aamantran portal, paying via UPI or debit card. Ensure to download the pass, check instructions, and be aware of enhanced security measures in place leading up to August 15.

item.title: Zerodha's Nikhil Kamath explores battery technologies that could power India's next manufacturing wave
item.description: In the latest episode of People by WTF, Nikhil Kamath sat down with Henning Rath, CEO of EnerVenue, and Kun Tang, Executive Chairman of HiNa Battery, to understand what the next battery industry could look like and whether India should build it.

item.title: Mint Explainer: Is India spending enough to protect its cultural heritage?
item.description: The ASI's expenditure on monument conservation, which peaked at ₹444 crore in FY24, has declined, even in popular tourist areas. This raises questions on India's ability to effectively conserve cultural heritage and attract foreign visitors, especially as arrivals decline.

item.title: Can a 'black hole star' solve the mystery of 'little red dots' spotted in the early Universe?
item.description: The black hole star, which dates from 660 million years after the Big Bang, was spotted by a US-led team of astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope.

item.title: Pakistan's fighter jets, supplied by USA, struggled against India during Operation Sindoor: Air Force veteran
item.description: In the 2025 conflict, Pakistan's ageing F-16 fighters, supplied by China, struggled with limited missile range against India’s advanced aircraft.

item.title: Quote of the day by Friedrich Nietzsche: ‘He who has a why to live can bear almost…’
item.description: Quote of the day by Friedrich Nietzsche talks about the importance of finding a reason to move through hardships in life. The quote has been popularised by Viktor Frankl.

item.title: Karnataka bandh called off after Kannada activists meet CM DK Shivakumar
item.description: The Cauvery water dispute remains a politically sensitive issue in Karnataka, with farmers' groups and Kannada organisations repeatedly staging protests over the matter.

item.title: Red Fort blast 2025 'officially attributed' to Al-Qaeda in Indian Subcontinent, says UNSC: what did its report reveal?
item.description: Red Fort blast 2025: The UNSC report said Al-Qaeda in Indian Subcontinent has evolved from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist organisation, strengthening its logistical and financial networks while operating through decentralised, small and dispersed cells.

item.title: Amid Imran Khan death rumours, what are the charges keeping Pakistan's former PM in jail?
item.description: A journalist's claims that senior Pakistani military officers feared Imran Khan may have died in custody sparked widespread rumours. Pakistan's military later rejected the reports as false and fabricated, saying the jailed former PM remains alive at Adiala Jail.

item.title: Ravi Kishan reveals what his wife told him amid social media frenzy: ‘Tumhe ghar mein lock kardenge’
item.description: Ravi Kishan's videos have sparked a meme fest across social media. Reacting to it, he said that he observed maun vrat (vow of silence).
